5.1 Multi-User Architecture – Overview

The ABpE Portal is designed for operation with thousands of users (estimated 23,000+ consultants). It uses Django's proven authentication and authorization system, extended with ABpE-specific data models.

5.2 The Django User Model

Django provides a fully equipped User model that offers all basic functions for authentication and authorization:

class User(models.Model):
    username = models.CharField(unique=True)
    password = models.CharField()  # hashed
    email = models.EmailField()
    first_name = models.CharField()
    last_name = models.CharField()
    is_active = models.BooleanField(default=True)
    is_staff = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    is_superuser = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    date_joined = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
    last_login = models.DateTimeField(null=True)
    groups = models.ManyToManyField(Group)
    user_permissions = models.ManyToManyField(Permission)

5.3 The ConsultantProfile – Extension for ABpE

For ABpE-specific data, the User model is extended with a ConsultantProfile (One-to-One relationship):

class ConsultantProfile(models.Model):
    user = models.OneToOneField(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    
    # Identification
    consultant_id = models.CharField(max_length=20, unique=True)
    title = models.CharField(max_length=50, blank=True)  # Dr., Prof., etc.
    
    # Contact data
    phone = models.CharField(max_length=50, blank=True)
    mobile = models.CharField(max_length=50, blank=True)
    address = models.TextField(blank=True)
    linkedin = models.URLField(blank=True)
    xing = models.URLField(blank=True)
    
    # CV data (as JSON for flexibility)
    cv_data = models.JSONField(default=dict)
    cv_last_updated = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)
    cv_public = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    
    # Status & Administration
    status = models.CharField(max_length=20, default='in_review')
    supervisor = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, null=True,
                                  related_name='supervised_consultants')
    
    # Timestamps
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
    updated_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)
    last_activity = models.DateTimeField(null=True, blank=True)

5.4 CVVersion – Version Management for CVs

Changes to CV data are versioned to maintain a history and track changes:

class CVVersion(models.Model):
    consultant = models.ForeignKey(ConsultantProfile, on_delete=models.CASCADE,
                                 related_name='cv_versions')
    version = models.IntegerField()
    cv_data = models.JSONField()
    changed_by = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.SET_NULL, null=True)
    change_note = models.CharField(max_length=255, blank=True)
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)
    
    class Meta:
        unique_together = ['consultant', 'version']
        ordering = ['-version']

5.5 UserSettings – User Settings

For UI-related settings such as theme and language, there is the UserSettings model:

class UserSettings(models.Model):
    user = models.OneToOneField(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    theme = models.CharField(max_length=10, default='system')
    language = models.CharField(max_length=5, default='de')
    sidebar_collapsed = models.BooleanField(default=False)

5.6 Roles and Groups

The permission structure is mapped via Django Groups. The following roles are defined:

RoleAccessCount (estimated)
ConsultantOwn CV editor, own profile~22,900
DispatcherEmail inbox, matching, search/filter consultants~50
SupervisorAll CVs of their consultants, create/edit consultants~30
AdminFull access, user management, system settings~5

5.7 Permission Checks in Views

In views, permissions are checked using Django decorators:

from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required, permission_required

@login_required
def dashboard(request):
    # Only logged-in users
    ...

@permission_required('cv_editor.view_own_cv')
def cv_editor(request):
    # Only users with the corresponding permission
    ...

5.8 Permission Checks in Templates

Permissions can also be checked in templates:

{% if perms.cv_editor.view_own_cv %}
    <a href="{% url 'cv_editor' %}">CV Editor</a>
{% endif %}

{% if user.is_staff %}
    <a href="/admin/">Admin</a>
{% endif %}

5.9 Registration Processes

For the 23,000+ consultants, three registration options are supported:

  • Self-registration: Consultant registers themselves, admin activates (or automatically)
  • CSV Import: Bulk import via Django Admin or Management Command
  • API Integration: External system (CRM) creates consultants via API

5.10 Security Aspects

The ABpE Portal relies on proven Django security mechanisms:

  • Passwords are hashed with PBKDF2 or bcrypt (no plaintext storage)
  • CSRF protection for all POST forms
  • XSS protection through template automatic escaping
  • SQL injection protection through Django ORM
  • Session cookies with HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite flags
  • Rate limiting for login attempts (django-axes)
